what: The autodiff divide VJP chain that the three-node `vjp_div_neg` group declines (a parameter numerator, so the divide's quotient is still read by the numerator's gradient) now runs its `multiply -> neg` tail as a second group, `tensor.fusion = "vjp_mul_neg"`: the tail reads the quotient the divide already stored, so the two tail operators become one pass and one buffer

before.note: the same source tree without the change, built clean; copied to /tmp/h299-base-install so both installs stay runnable

programs.chain: test/cases/perf/fusion_chain.cml --arg fused=0: the declined program alone (sum of a parameter tensor divided by a parameter vector)
programs.step: test/cases/perf/fusion_step.cml --arg fused=0 --arg lr=0.01: the same declined chain inside a training step

method.timing: each process reports ms_per_step from inside its loop; the two installs are run alternately (the second-installed side runs first on odd pairs) so a drifting host falls on both sides of a pair
method.null_control: two copies of the *before* install compared through the same loop: it measures what the host alone does to a pair of identical builds, and bounds every difference the change can claim

load_average.note: the host runs other tenants' work throughout; a separate 19-core job keeps the load above 50 and swings it by a factor of two between runs

operator_calls_per_step.note: the two tail operators are replaced by the group pass, which the node VM runs inside the neg node; the divide still runs, which is the point: the tail reads its stored value

operator_share_of_the_step_before.note: upper bound of what a one-buffer-saving fusion can remove at 1M: the group still reads both operands and writes one buffer, so the saving is the intermediate buffer's traffic, not two passes of work

deterministic_evidence.bytes: test/plans/feat/modules/fusion_group.plan.toml pins gradient.w bytes equal between std::nvm (group runs) and std::fvm (no kernel: the two operators run) in the default mode and under std::opt safe_fp=true; the pair is one multiply rounding and one sign flip in the operators' order, so it takes no numeric licence

conclusion: The change removes two operator calls per declined step (multiply and neg) and the profile counts prove it, but this host at load 87-105 cannot resolve the time it saves: the smallest per-pair change (0.006 ms at 131k in the step) is far below the host's own spread, and a pair of identical builds moves by up to 2.5 ms at 1M. The one number that points the right way is the chain's minimum at 131k (0.452 -> 0.431 ms, -4.6%); every larger case is inside the noise, in both directions. A quiet host is needed to put a percentage on the one buffer the pass saves; the operator counts and the byte equality do not depend on the host and are pinned by the plan.
